candidates.rationale: Numerator mixes adjusted $close with raw $low/$high (repo confirms $close is overwritten to adj_close while open/high/low stay raw), a scale bug that imports forward-looking dividend adjustments into a same-day range position and likely underlies both the near-gate 0.792 archive correlation and the late-sample IC fade (2012: 0.0027, 2013: 0.0010). Swapped the $close leaf for $open, keeping the range term all-raw.

Same scale bug as its sibling: numerator ($high - $close) mixes raw high with adjusted close while the denominator is all-raw, plausibly contributing to the lone negative year (2013: -0.0023) behind the stability=0.93 flag. Swapped $close to $open in the numerator only.

The static CS_RANK($roe) leg is weakest in exactly the post-crash junk-rally years (2003: 0.0005, 2009: 0.0066, 2010: 0.0023), when a flat profitability-level tilt lags. Swapped $roe for $accrual_gap, an earnings-quality measure rather than a profitability level, leaving the value leg untouched.

The subtracted TS_MEAN($return,10) leg drives both the weak 2009-2011 patch (0.0039/0.0015/0.0056) and the 0.780 correlation with 0168481b31dce7bc, which shares this exact subtree. Lengthened its window to 21 to damp the post-crash short-term reversal whipsaw.

Only parent charged for complexity (0.100 of fitness) and the set's lowest coverage (0.934), both driven by the 4th field / extra subtraction term pushing depth to 5/6. Removed the '- TS_MEAN($return, 5)' term, returning to 3 fields and depth 4/6.

Sits at rho 0.780 against 693246746bbdc073, sharing both an EPS/price value leg and the 10-day return leg (the latter already reworked in that parent's mutation). Swapped the value leg's fundamental to $book_per_share to separate the two lineages instead of re-touching the shared momentum leg.
TS_MAX($high,21) - $close mixes raw high with adjusted close, the same scale bug as in 97dfe9ddfd2178f6, and may explain the lone negative year (2013: -0.0028). Swapped $close for $open.

Set-worst turnover (0.294, charged 0.011) and shortest half-life (3.0 days): the fast TS_DELTA($open,5) leg churns ranks daily against the much slower TS_STD(63)/TS_STD(5) leg it's multiplied with. Lengthened the delta window to 21 to match time-scales and cut churn, keeping the vol-term-structure x price-delta shape this round's working memory flags as valuable (not filler).
Second-shortest half-life (4.1 days), third-highest turnover (0.193), and the set's largest single-year miss (2012: -0.0063) all trace to the fast TS_MEAN($return,5) leg. Lengthened it to 21.

Largest regime break in the set: 2003 swings to -0.0068, consistent with the bare $earnings_per_share leg (unscaled by price or share count, so it doubles as a no-split/size proxy) fighting a liquidity-dislike leg during a junk-led rebound rally. Left EPS alone to avoid duplicating 0168481b31dce7bc's EPS/close subtree; lengthened the dollar-volume window from 21 to 63 to damp sensitivity to that transient spike.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Swapping the aggregator on one term (TS_MIN vs TS_MEAN on $low,21) barely moved correlation (rho 0.997). A same-window aggregator swap on a single term won't clear the correlation gate.
  2. Smoothing a slow fundamental with a long TS_MEAN (roa, 126d) stayed near-identical to the raw field (rho 0.837) since fundamentals update quarterly. Pair fundamentals with a fast-moving second term rather than just smoothing them.
  3. Wrapping one operand of a ratio in CS_RANK ($dollar_volume ranked inside TS_MEAN) didn't decorrelate from the unranked version (rho 0.911). Adding a rank around a sub-term is a weak move against the correlation gate.
  4. EMA-crossover forms correlate highly across window choices and ratio-vs-difference framing (rho 0.825 between two differently-windowed variants this round). Treat EMA-crossover as one already-covered family, not new proposals per window pair.
  5. A volatility-term-structure ratio (long-window TS_STD over short-window TS_STD of one field) crossed with that same field's own short TS_DELTA scored this round's top fitness (6.583) as pure price, beating every fundamental-crossed accept. Do not treat this shape as low-value filler like plain OHLC levels/returns.
  6. Swapping only the top-level combinator (* vs -) between two otherwise-identical CS_RANK legs still shares the full subtree (4 nodes) and gets rejected. Change a leg's field, window, or wrapper too, not just how the legs combine.
  7. Swapping a single OHLC leaf while leaving an identical guarded denominator/wrapper in place shares nearly the whole tree (6-7+ nodes). Vary two structural pieces at once when reusing an archived shape, not just the one leaf.
  8. A 252-day window failed coverage (0.874) on a plain price field ($close), matching the fundamental failure range exactly. Treat ~252-day lookbacks as a coverage risk for any field, not just sparse fundamentals.
  9. Every cheap_screen reject this round was a price/return/volume-only combination (|t| 0.17-0.57, 4 for 4). A fundamental leg is still required to clear the cheap screen at all, not just to score well later.
  10. Adding an extra multiplicative TS_RANK(volume) factor to an existing two-leg expression, even combined with an overall sign flip, kept correlation at 0.976 against the original. Bolting on a volume-rank multiplier is not a reliable way to decorrelate from an archived idea.
  11. Inserting a smoothing wrapper (e.g. TS_MEAN) around just one leaf of a multi-term product, leaving the rest of the structure untouched, still shared 6 of the tree's nodes. Wrap at least two legs, or change the outer combinator too.
  12. About a third of this round's rejects were in-run duplicates, clustered in two templates: open/high/low range-position ratios and EPS-times-dollar-volume-rank ratios. Deprioritize further variations of these two families next round.
